name: Question 9
worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+{30}^{∘})-2 & =0 \\ 4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+{30}^{∘}) & =2 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+{30}^{∘}) & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+{30}^{∘} & ={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & 3x+{30}^{∘} & ={300}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & ={60}^{∘}-{30}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} & \, & \, & 3x & ={300}^{∘}-{30}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} \\ 3x & ={30}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} & \, & \, & 3x & ={270}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} \\ x & ={10}^{∘}+n\cdot {120}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={90}^{∘}+n\cdot {120}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={10}^{∘}$ and $x={90}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x={130}^{∘}$ and $x={210}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x={250}^{∘}$ and $x={330}^{∘}.$

All other integer values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$  

So, in ascending order, the solutions are

$$
{x}_{1}={10}^{∘},\,{x}_{2}={90}^{∘},\,{x}_{3}={130}^{∘},\,{x}_{4}={210}^{∘},\,{x}_{5}={250}^{∘},\,{x}_{6}={330}^{∘}.
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we rearrange the equation as follows: 4cos⁡(3x+30∘)−2=04cos⁡(3x+30∘)=2cos⁡(3x+30∘)=12

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

3x+30∘=60∘+n⋅360∘,3x+30∘=300∘+n⋅360∘.

Solving the two equations above for x gives: 3x=60∘−30∘+n⋅360∘3x=300∘−30∘+n⋅360∘3x=30∘+n⋅360∘3x=270∘+n⋅360∘x=10∘+n⋅120∘x=90∘+n⋅120∘

We set n=0,±1,±2,…, until we have generated all solutions in the domain 0∘≤x<360∘.

  • Setting n=0 gives x=10∘ and x=90∘.

  • Setting n=1 gives x=130∘ and x=210∘.

  • Setting n=2 gives x=250∘ and x=330∘.

All other integer values of n generate solutions outside the domain 0∘≤x<360∘.

So, in ascending order, the solutions are x1=10∘,x2=90∘,x3=130∘,x4=210∘,x5=250∘,x6=330∘.
